plain: Took in, as ideas or feelings

webster.text: Drank in, as a fluid; absorbed; received into the mind and retained.

example.quote: Believe me, my countrymen, they have imbibed an opinion on the other side the water, that we are an ignorant, a timid, and a stupid people; nay, their tools on this side have often the impudence to dispute your bravery.
example.cite: John Adams, A Dissertation on the Canon and the Feudal Law (1765)
